source_fidelity_repair_note: SOURCE_FIDELITY_REPAIR: Stem text restored verbatim from registry.json. Previous scrape inverted spring anchor to top and corrupted geometry. Original geometry: spring (k, unstretched length R) attached to bottom of vertical circular hoop (radius R). Bead released from top (y1 = 2R, spring length 2R, extension x1 = R). Bead moves until spring length becomes R (forming an equilateral triangle with bottom anchor and circle center; central angle 60 deg from vertical bottom, height y2 = R - R cos(60 deg) = R/2, drop Delta h = 3R/2). Spring relaxes to extension x2 = 0. Potential energy loss: Delta U_grav = mg(3R/2) and Delta U_spring = 1/2 k R^2. By energy conservation: 1/2 m v^2 = 3/2 mgR + 1/2 k R^2 => v^2 = 3gR + k R^2 / m => v = sqrt(3gR + k R^2 / m) [Option B]. Preserved on HOLD awaiting verified official diagram asset and key.

candidate_solve.assumed_parameters_from_coaching_figure: Bead on vertical circular hoop (radius R). Spring (stiffness k, unstretched length R) attached to bottom of hoop. Bead released from top.
candidate_solve.derivation: Initial state (top of hoop): y1 = 2R, spring length = 2R, extension x1 = 2R - R = R, v1 = 0. Final state (length of spring becomes R): spring anchor at bottom (0,0), hoop center at (0,R), bead at P on circle. Since distance from bottom to P is R, and from center to P is R, triangle formed by bottom anchor, center, and P is equilateral with side R. The angle at center from downward vertical is 60 deg. Height of P: y2 = R - R cos(60 deg) = R - R/2 = R/2. Height drop: Delta h = y1 - y2 = 2R - R/2 = 3R/2. Final spring extension x2 = R - R = 0 (spring is unstretched). Energy conservation: 1/2 m v^2 = mg(Delta h) + 1/2 k x1^2 - 1/2 k x2^2 = mg(3R/2) + 1/2 k R^2 - 0 = 3/2 mgR + 1/2 k R^2. Multiplying by 2/m: v^2 = 3gR + (k R^2 / m) => v = sqrt(3gR + (k R^2 / m)).
candidate_solve.limiting_cases: If k = 0 (pure gravity), v = sqrt(2 g Delta h) = sqrt(2 g * 3R/2) = sqrt(3gR). If g = 0 (pure spring), v = sqrt(k R^2 / m). Both conservative forces lose potential energy simultaneously, yielding Option B.
